name: IL-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's +19 Democratic partisan lean in a deep-blue Chicago-area seat
Daniel Biss's strong fundraising (~$2.9M) versus a Republican opponent with no reported finances
Prediction markets price Democratic win probability near 97%
Open seat after Schakowsky's retirement, but no evidence of a competitive general election
model.rationale: The seat's +19 Democratic lean, Biss's dominant fundraising edge, and markets pricing a Democratic win at roughly 97% all point to a safe Democratic hold despite the open seat. No polls or expert ratings suggest any meaningful Republican opening.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the Republican nominee within single digits, or a major outside-spending surge against Biss, would be the first sign this is closer than fundamentals indicate.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jan Schakowsky (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jan Schakowsky's retirement leaves this Chicago-area district open, but the seat remains one of the most Democratic-leaning House districts in the country, with a partisan lean of about +19 points Democratic. Daniel Biss enters the general election with roughly $2.9 million raised and substantial outside spending on both sides, while Republican John Elleson shows no reported fundraising or cash on hand in available records.

Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability near 97%, and no general-election polls or expert ratings indicate a competitive race. The forecast treats this as a safe Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
